Neutral-mass voting within one feature group

Source: R/adducts.R
neutralMassVote.Rd

neutralMassVote() is the core of annotateAdducts() for a single group of features. Every feature is tried as every quasi-molecular ion (quasi == 1). A neutral mass is a hypothesis when at least one other feature is explained by some rule as an ion of the same mass. Duplicate hypotheses (same features with the same rules) are merged, and the rest are ranked by summed rule score (ips), then by explained intensity.

Usage

neutralMassVote(mz, intensity, rules, ppm = 10, mzabs = 0.005)

Arguments

mz

numeric m/z values of the group's features.

intensity

numeric representative intensities of the features.

rules

data.frame with rules in CAMERA's format.

ppm

numeric(1) relative tolerance in ppm.

mzabs

numeric(1) absolute tolerance.

Value

data.frame with one row per hypothesis and member feature and the columns feature (index into mz), hypothesis (rank), M, adduct, n_ions, score and intensity.

Examples

mz <- c(124.0392, 152.0342, 170.0445, 192.0275, 377.0300)
neutralMassVote(mz, c(81, 50, 100, 11, 2), defaultAdductRules())
